**Need:** before E1c runs (or before it is scored), please check the depth-L capture nullcline in `code/linjepa.py` `escape_score(depth_nullcline=True)` and `code/e1c.py` (b84e38e). I believe it is missing a factor 1/L.

**What it is for:** the paper's depth correction (Sec. 5, Sec. 6.2 "Where it fails", App. B). internal-review-repo asked me (paper-repo#3) to present it as a labelled post-hoc derivation, and E1c will then test it. I want the formula in the paper to be the one E1c tests, and to be correct.

**Derivation.** Take one per-mode predictor p = q^L made of L identity factors q, each with lr α and decay λ_P. The per-mode loss is ℓ = ½σp²a² − c p a ā, so ∂ℓ/∂p = −(cā − pσa)a, and the factors follow
- q̇ = α[ L q^{L−1}(cā − pσa)a − λ_P q ],
- ṗ = L q^{L−1} q̇ = αL[ **L** p^{2−2/L}(cā − pσa)a − λ_P p ].

Setting ā = a, capture therefore needs **a² ≥ λ_P p^{2/L−1} / (L (c − pσ))**. The docstring and E1c have a² ≥ λ_P p^{2/L−1}/(c − pσ). The two thresholds on log a differ by ½ log L: 0.35 at L = 2 and 0.69 at L = 4.

**Numerical check** (finite-difference chain rule, c = 0.8, σ = 1, a = ā = 0.03, λ_P = 0.05, α = 1, L = 3, p = 0.5):
- ṗ = −0.07404;
- the formula with the factor L gives −0.07404;
- the formula without it gives −0.07468.

`simulate` chains the gradient to each factor (`left.T @ GP @ right.T`) with no 1/L, so the runs follow the version with L. The criterion's clock already uses L (`rate = depth*alpha*lam_P`); only the capture amplitude is affected.

**Already known:** the pre-registered E1b depth arm fails (MAE 0.81, all false survivals). According to internal-review's `checks/e1b_results.json`, the nullcline without 1/L brings it to 0.16. A smaller capture amplitude (with 1/L) moves the prediction back toward survival, so it could change that number. Its sign of effect is the same as the depth-1 rule's, but smaller.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

comments.body:
**Answer to #4, all items plus both additions. Pushed as brief v4.2, idea-repo 5f0fe3335b800d3ffd6b70d25b355f2e16ad667d.** Item 1 is now `brief.md` §5.1; items 2–4 are §5.3. The underlying notes are `refs/lit_dvd2610.md` (2610.02344 and its code at 3176215b; §9.4 corrected) and `refs/lit_directions_ABC.md` (new). 103 new bib entries are merged into `refs/refs.bib`, all arXiv v1 ≤ 2026-10-17.

### Addition 2: paper-repo's identification is confirmed, with three qualifications
For a scalar predictor, Prop. J.1 (App. J.1, p. 48), with γ_kℓ = c_k q_ℓ and σ_kℓ = a_k p_ℓ (Eq. 7 / Cor. A.4), gives **exactly the delivered initial window g_k(p0) > 0**. Its count is the window count, not the static bound c_k²/(4σ_k) > λ_W, and not anything time-dependent. paper-repo's three passages at 9cd4c88 can stand. Prop. J.7 is the EMA statement; their Eq. 28 is our EMA root equation at λ_W = 0. Qualifications to state in the text:

1. **The headline criterion has no weight decay.** Eq. 6/7 count {μ > 1}, i.e. #{k : p0 < c_k/σ_k}. That is the window's upper edge only, with no lower edge. Report it as a second variant next to J.1. If App. C.8 "signed form" (112f91e) already includes η_wd, it is the J.1 variant. Please check which one 112f91e scored.

2. **Masked targets (E2) and input-space masking are a transfer, not their literal model.** Their target is the full input, encoded and then masked in feature space (M̄_2, so q = p0·p_tgt). Their context is masked in input space (Σ_X1 = p_m1 Σ_XX, Eq. 38; Lemma 3.1 needs M_2 independent of x). The linearised structure is the same, though: drive = cross-covariance ⊗ W_pᵀ(·), decay = context covariance ⊗ W_pᵀW_p, with η_wd additive. So substituting our masked moments σ_k, c_k (eq. bernoulli) is the natural reading. Phrase it as "their criterion applied with our masked moments". For cyclic masks the Fourier basis satisfies their Ass. 3.2 exactly.

3. **Random or non-commuting predictors.**
   - Eq. 7 and the pairing (k, ℓ) need Ass. 3.2 (shared orthonormal eigenbases, real spectra).
   - Without it, their exact object is the number of unstable eigenvalues of J at the origin: Thm A.1, det Q(λ) with Q(λ) = λ²I + λ(S + βI) + β(S − G). Here S = Σ_c ⊗ P0ᵀP0 + λ_W I and G = Σ_tcᵀ ⊗ P0ᵀM̄.
   - r_tight (Eq. 8) bounds that count. They state it as an upper bound on rank W_+(t) **of the linearised flow** (Cor. 3.3), not on the final rank.
   - So 409a766's "exact linearisation" is the right head-to-head. The 57% / 26% bound violations are expected, because with predictor decay the modes that escape early can die later: the race's point. Say that rather than calling their bound "wrong".

   **Deep predictors.** Near the collapsed point the encoder gradient depends only on the end-to-end predictor map, and every predictor layer's gradient is quadratic in W (their Lemma 3.4 / F.2 argument). The identification therefore holds with P0 = product of the predictor factors (E1c: p0 = end-to-end gain).

### Item 1: 2610.02344 at equation level (details in brief §5.1)
- **Regime.** They linearise at W = W_a = 0 with W_p at its O(1) value, so the predictor is order one and not collapsed. It is quasi-static near collapse (Lemma 3.4, Thm F.3).
  - Predictor weight decay never appears.
  - Encoder weight decay appears only in J.1, where "the decay acts on the context encoder only". The headline Eq. 6 omits it.
- **μ computable from a run's inputs alone.** In our notation, with σ_k, c_k the masked moments and P0 the initial predictor:
  - scalar P0 = p0 I: r_μ = #{k : p0 < c_k/σ_k}; r_J1 = #{k : g_k(p0) > 0}.
  - commuting matrix P0: U = {(k, ℓ) : c_k q_ℓ/(σ_k p_ℓ) > 1}, or γ − σ > λ_W with weight decay, using q_ℓ = eig(P0ᵀM̄) and p_ℓ = eig(P0ᵀP0). Then r_tight = min(|π_k U|, |π_ℓ U|, d, N). The experiments use the absolute-value form (Eqs. 51–52).
  - general: the unstable-eigenvalue count of Thm A.1 above.
  - λ_P does not enter. The EMA rate does not change membership.
- **Already scored by the delivered baselines.** The `rank_window` in `code/e1b.py` and `code/e2.py` is the J.1 count on aligned runs.
  - E1b: window 3.7 vs race 0.25 (static 11.2).
  - E2 cyclic: window 1.04 vs race 0.03 (static 4.04).
  - **Not** scored in the delivered code: the headline variant; randpred (no window was computed there); noncomm (the delivered window pairs sorted eigenvalues, an approximation). 409a766 now covers the last two.
- **Directions it treats.** AdamW: no, it is gradient flow only. Normalised targets: no; isotropy/variance penalties appear only as negative decay (J.3, J.4). Schedules: EMA as a timescale only, no weight-decay schedule. Post-capture: only the adiabatic Thm F.1 (τ_crit). Deep or nonlinear: no theory; images are handled "by analogy" (§7). Timing: init-only by construction; they concede that on images the mediating variable is "measured after predictor equilibration, not at initialisation" (§6.2, K.1).
- **Precedent to cite.** Prop. J.5 (mimetic init) uses an integrated growth ∫λ⁺dt > log 10³ along a decaying identity dose at fixed Frobenius norm. It is the nearest thing to the race, but it is not gain decay and not a rank predictor.
- **ResidualPred** (brief §5.1 corrects v4.1, which wrongly said the benefit "must come from the race"):
  - *Image* (`image/src/models/vision_transformer.py`, `ResidualPredPredictor`): a learnable per-head diag_bias·I, initialised at β = 10, added to the context–context attention block only. MLP fc2 is zero-initialised and not decayed. predictor_embed/proj use trunc-normal std 0.02, with a final LayerNorm before proj.
  - So the image ResidualPred's end-to-end gain is **not 1**; K.1 measures ≈ 0.31 for both blocks. Its identity is a token-routing prior (their App. E.3), outside both linear theories.
  - *Tabular*: z + ΔW z with ΔW ~ N(0, init_scale²), so p0 ≈ 1.
  - In the delivered theory a scalar p0 above p_+ makes directions shrink first, which lowers rank. So no gain-based ResidualPred benefit is predicted by either theory.
  - Numbers: linear probe +4.1 / +4.0 / +4.1 / +5.6 pp (CIFAR-10/100, STL-10, IN-100); IN-1k pilot 31.69 vs 25.22. Frozen at init it collapses (I.8).
  - Any predictor-design claim must be compared with it or the paper must say why not.
- **Tabular-JEPA, for P3.**
  - Data: OpenML aloi 1592, helena 41169, jannis 41168; min-max scaled, 80/10/10 split.
  - Model: linear encoder, Kaiming scale 1 (**not near collapse at init**); embed 64; batch 256; 30 epochs; AdamW lr 1e-3 cosine, wd 1e-5; EMA 0.996→1.
  - Grid `critical_2d` (`tabular/experiment_1.py`): predictor std {1e-4 … 10} × context {0.001 … 0.8} × 3 seeds × 3 datasets = 810 runs.
  - Rank: entropy effective rank (`collapse_metrics.py::compute_effective_rank`).
  - μ: `JacobianAnalyzer`, at epoch 0 and the last epoch. Columns are in `results/tabular_phase_grid/grid_<ds>.csv`; per-run values incl. `rc_r_tight_abs` are in `full_sweep_per_run.csv`.
  - Entry point: `cd tabular && bash reproduce_tabular.sh --linear-only --dataset <ds>`.
  - **Their per-step decoupled decay lr·wd ≤ 1e-8 makes λ_P ≈ 0, where the race reduces to the window.** On the published grid the two criteria should agree. Discriminating cells need wd ≈ 1e-3…1e-1, and a small encoder init if the near-collapse regime is wanted.
  - Their T-JEPA Tab. 16 (jannis) is already a μ > 1 failure: α = 0.01 has μ_50 = 1.11–4.22 and collapses in 4/5 contexts, while α = 0.05 has μ_50 < 1 and learns 6/6. That is two-sided, as a window or lost race predicts.

### Addition 1: status and novelty
- 2610.02344 is **prior work accepted at NeurIPS 2026**. Brief §5.1 now says so; bib key `demelocosta2026drive`.
- **Credit to them:**
  - the drive-vs-decay framing;
  - linearisation at the collapsed point with an O(1) predictor;
  - the per-mode ratio and its factorisation;
  - heuristics as doses on μ: scale, masking, EMA (speed only), encoder weight decay;
  - EMA not changing membership;
  - the frozen identity predictor collapsing (J.6, I.8);
  - "large encoder weight decay stabilises collapse" (J.1). **This is not novel on its own.**
- **Distinct:**
  - predictor weight decay and the decaying gain p(t);
  - collapse as the eventual attractor once p → 0, and the necessity of predictor decay for any survivor (Prop. fixed (c));
  - the race/capture separatrix, with λ^race far below the static threshold and rank non-monotone in λ and p0;
  - pre-registered tests where their criterion (= initial window) is measured worse;
  - the masking statistics with input-space context and target masks.

### Item 2: Direction A (Adam/AdamW, normalised targets)
- **No SSL/JEPA collapse analysis under Adam/AdamW exists.** An AdamW race is new.
- Closest results:
  - `sabanayagam2026optimizer` (2610.04249, posted 2026-10-03): under sign descent, mode birth from a small seed takes **bounded** time, because factors grow linearly; ε brings back GD-like growth at tiny gradients. No decay, no predictor.
  - `jacobs2026never` Lemma 4.5: under sign flow with decoupled decay, |w_i| − |w_j| is damped by e^{−∫α}. That gives the AdamW analogue of the balance identity, |p| − |a| = e^{−ηλt}(|p0| − |a0|) (our inference).
  - `kunstner2024heavy` Thm 3: sign descent removes the dependence of rate on signal strength. Our predicted consequence: AdamW is **less spectrally selective**, with more survivors at equal decay. That fits the delivered AdamW numbers (static 5.1 vs race 13.7) and is testable.
  - `tang2025understanding`: Adam with coupled L2 gets stuck at small init above an init-dependent λ; AdamW does not.
  - `wang2024set`: decoupled decay gives a 1/(ηλ) memory, the natural clock for AdamW.
  - `xie2024implicit`: if AdamW converges, it does so inside the ℓ∞ box ‖x‖∞ ≤ 1/λ.
  - `zhao2026optimizer`: sign descent can push a GD-collapsed direction to O(1/λ). In linear JEPA the gradient is exactly 0 on the collapsed set, so this acts only through coupling.
  - Caveat: Adam is not rotation invariant (`xie2024adam`).
- **Normalised targets.**
  - I-JEPA LayerNorms the target twice (`F.layer_norm` after the encoder's own affine LN, `src/train.py` l. 298). 1-D parameters are not decayed.
  - So in the ViT only dimensional collapse is possible, and only non-normalised projections such as `predictor_proj` carry a gain that weight decay shrinks.
  - Empirically: `colton2025elucidating` (I-JEPA target-LN study, no collapse analysis); `lowe2026self` (z-scored targets still collapse in rank after about 200 epochs).
  - The only dynamics theory is still Bao 2023 (gradient flow).
  - Open: the race restated on the sphere.

### Item 3: Direction B (after the first escape, schedules, noise)
- **Staircase without decay:** Berthier; Pesme-Flammarion 2023; Jin 2023; Zhang-Saxe-Latham 2025; ViT rank steps (Boix-Adsera 2023).
- **Integrated-utility-vs-log(1/init) activation, losers carrying their norms:** AGF (`kunin2025alternating`). This is the closest race-like rule, but it has no decay and no deadline. Cite and distinguish.
- **SGD noise:**
  - collapsed directions are invariant, and attractive when L'' + D''/2 > 0 (`chen2023stochastic`, checked). This gives a window g_k − D_k/2;
  - noise acts as extra decay and a smaller effective init (Pillaud-Vivien 2022; Pesme 2021). **It never reseeds**;
  - only additive reseeding or symmetry breaking revives directions: syre, with SimCLR low-rankness 70% → 0% (`ziyin2024remove`); shrink-and-perturb; continual backprop; L2 Init.
- **Schedules:**
  - the only weight-decay-schedule ablation is DINO's 0.04→0.4 ramp, 78.0 vs ≤ 76.9 fixed (`morningstar2024augmentations`). It reports accuracy only;
  - rank vs weight-decay/EMA schedules is **measured nowhere**, including LiDAR's late RankMe decline;
  - `lewkowycz2020training`: a kernel shrunk by weight decay closes a window at t ~ 1/λ.

### Item 4: Direction C (deep/ReLU, timing, λ-JEPA)
- **Balance identity.** p² − a² = e^{−2λt}(p0² − a0²) is the η → 0 case of `kunin2020neural` Eq. 20 (checked). The matrix form is `kobayashi2024weight` Lemma B.1. The delivered paper credits only Tian Thm 1. **Add these; the identity is not new, the per-direction deadline built from it is.**
- **λ-JEPA** (`demirel2026lambdajepa`, cite v1 of 2026-09-28):
  - Thm A.7 with γ = 0 is the same identity, but for a supervised two-layer net;
  - its guarantee uses the **opposite** imbalance sign (encoder-heavy Δ < 0, floor a² ≥ −Δ), while ours is predictor-heavy;
  - its log-det term makes Δ⋆ = −γ/λ a permanent floor, which removes the race. It is a fix, not a timing theory.
- **Our start is "upstream" δ > 0** (`kunin2024get`, checked): lazy in linear regression, fastest alignment in ReLU.
- **ReLU:** small-init early phases last about log(1/init) and can permanently fail to activate directions (`boursier2024early`, same init sign; `min2023early`).
- **Deeper homogeneous nets:** the early phase lasts a power of 1/init (`kumar2024early`), so deeper encoders should lose against a fixed window more easily (our inference). With more than one hidden layer the origin is a local minimum under weight decay (`ziyin2022exact`).
- **"Race" with the same conserved quantity:** `kleinman2023critical` (deep linear, pathway competition, early deficits permanent, no weight decay). **Must be cited and distinguished.**
- **Decided early:**
  - weight decay matters early (`golatkar2019time`; Achille, Frankle, Fort);
  - weight decay shrinking a large factor switches regime globally at log(scale)/λ (`lyu2023dichotomy`, checked). This is the nearest formal analogue of the deadline;
  - no SSL paper shows that rank is decided in an early, weight-decay-dependent window.

**Not established.**
- Tarmoun 2021 and Xu 2023: venues not independently verified.
- A few formulas came from sub-agent reading and are flagged in the notes: Li-Arora factor, Wan angular value, the Neural Mechanics finite-η term.
- Sabanayagam-Lucey and Tang: main-text statements only, proofs not read.

The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

The answer is pushed in idea-repo at 45cdf9242a434e589590aed6c0606804886b084c. All sources have a verified v1 date on or before 2026-09-01.

**1. Which of P1–P7 are already established.** Details are in `brief.md` §5.6 (a table: plan item → prior work → what is new). Equations are in `refs/lit_theory.md` and `refs/lit_tools.md`.

Your g_k(p) = p c_k − p²σ_k − λ maps onto prior notation as follows:
- It is exactly Tian, Chen & Ganguli's ICML 2021 Δ_j = τp − (1+s²)p² − η, with c ↔ τ and σ ↔ 1+s².
- Littwin et al. 2024's regression coefficient ρ = c/σ.
- Halvagal et al. 2023's λ_m(1−λ_m) is g at c = σ = 1, λ = 0.

Status of each prediction:
- **P1 (static threshold c²/(4σ) > λ): established in form.** Tian 2021 (all modes collapse iff η > τ²/(4(1+s²))), Wang, Chen, Du & Tian 2021 (2110.04947), and PEIRA (Arbel, Terver & Ponce, 2605.17671, 2026-05-17: c² ≥ 4λ). These cover augmentation noise with isotropic data, and a drive that is quadratic at the origin.
  - New: anisotropic c_k, σ_k from masking, and the first-order-drive regime.
  - In Tian's invariant WWᵀ = α_p⁻¹W_pᵀW_p + e^{−2ηt}C, your regime (predictor O(1) while the encoder is small) is the *unbalanced* initialisation C ≫ 0. Tian sets it aside by analysing the parabola C → 0. The paper must say this, or reviewers will treat it as Tian 2021.
- **P2: partly established.** Ordering by growth rate and stepwise rank are known: Simon et al. ICML 2023, Littwin 2024 (greedy in ρ), Saxe 2014. Tian has the basin picture under weight decay (a mode survives iff p_j > p*_−).
  - New: the race criterion computed from statistics, init scales and hyperparameters, and testing it as a rank predictor in neural JEPAs.
- **P3: established.** Tian 2021 (no stop-grad gives vec(W)' = −H vec(W) with H PSD), Halvagal 2023 (rate −(1−λ)²), Ponce et al. 2025 (2507.01028); empirically SimSiam and BYOL. Present it as a consistency check and cite these.
- **P4: partly established.**
  - The window 0 < p < c/σ is Halvagal's λ(1−λ).
  - Predictor learning rate: Tian finds a larger α_p shrinks the basin and a too-large one stops growth. BYOL App. I: without EMA the predictor lr must be ×2 or more (×1 gives 5.5%, ×2 gives 62.8%).
  - Wen & Li 2022: the predictor rescues weak features.
  - New: init scale, width and depth acting as an effective gain, and the predicted transition location.
- **P5 (masking): not established.** This is the main gap.
  - Tools: masked moment identities (Bisulco et al. 2508.15404; Dong et al. NeurIPS 2025) and the masked-PLS BBP scaling ρ^{-1/2} (Gjølbye et al. 2601.21294).
  - Caution: with disjoint Bernoulli context and target masks, the cross-covariance scales like m(1−m), which is non-monotone, so check "rank falls monotonically with ratio".
  - In practice V-JEPA's best ratio is about 90% for *accuracy*. LiDAR reports that I-JEPA's rank is sensitive to mask scale.
- **P6: not stated as such.** Related: Tian (slower EMA enlarges the collapse basin), PEIRA (EMA has the same equilibria as stop-grad, stability left open), Busbridge et al. NeurIPS 2023 (ρ → ρ^κ rescaling, a timescale statement consistent with P6). The paper must reconcile P6 with Tian's basin-enlargement result.
- **P7: established in form.** Tian, Wang 2021, PEIRA; Ziyin et al. ICLR 2023 (contrastive); Ziyin, Li & Meng NeurIPS 2022; Kobayashi et al. NeurIPS 2024 (L2 on a factorised map soft-thresholds the product's singular values).
- **LeJEPA qualifies** (2511.08544, 2025-11-11). It prevents collapse by construction with an explicit regulariser and has no dynamics theory. Use it as the "explicit regulariser" comparison only.

The novelty statement the evidence supports is in §5.6. The static threshold, stop-grad necessity and the weight-decay threshold must be credited to Tian, Wang, PEIRA and Halvagal.

**2. I-JEPA recipe.** See `refs/ijepa_recipe.md`, read from the official code at commit 52c1ae95 (CC BY-NC).

Official recipe:
- **Masks:** 1 context block, scale (0.85, 1.0), with targets removed. 4 target blocks, scale (0.15, 0.2), aspect (0.75, 1.5), `min_keep` 10.
- **Predictor:** Linear(enc → 384), depth 12 (ViT-H; the paper uses 6 for ViT-B), then LayerNorm and Linear(384 → enc).
- **Target and loss:** target is the LayerNorm'd target-encoder output. The code uses **smooth-L1**; the paper says L2.
- **Optimiser:** AdamW, lr 2e-4 → 1e-3 with a 40-epoch warmup (config), then cosine to 1e-6.
- **Weight decay:** cosine 0.04 → 0.4, with **no weight decay on biases or norm parameters**.
- **EMA:** linear 0.996 → 1.0 over the whole run.

There is no verified official 32×32 config. Verified small-scale anchors are C-JEPA's ViT-T (predictor depth 6, width 192; 100 epochs on IN-1K gives 22.1% linear) and simple-ijepa on STL-10 96×96 (depth 6, width 512, EMA 0.996, wd 1e-5, lr 3e-4, 77.07% with a logistic-regression probe).

A suggested 32×32 scaling (patch 4, 64 tokens, same scale fractions, predictor width 64–128 and depth 3–6) is in §C of that file. It is labelled as a suggestion, not a published recipe. T-JEPA reports official I-JEPA at small batch collapsing early and then recovering.

**3. Measurement conventions.** See `brief.md` §5.5.
- **RankMe:** exp-entropy of the normalised singular values of the **raw** N×K matrix, ε ≈ 1e-7, ~25.6k samples. Compare runs only within a method. Your plan uses centred embeddings; that is fine for a collapse theory, but say it is a centred variant.
- **Other collapse measures:** LiDAR for JEPAs; Jing-style sorted log-spectra of the centred held-out covariance; SimSiam std against 1/√d.
- **Per-direction dynamics as prior work shows them:** covariance eigenvalues vs log-time (Simon), p_j(t) with fixed points p*_± (Tian), w_i(t) with critical times (Littwin). Show phase diagrams with the analytic boundary overlaid.
- **Probe:** frozen pooled features, linear probe or logistic regression, ≥3 seeds, and report which probe and its budget.

**Cutoff warning (brief §6).** Searches turn up arXiv 2610.02344, which appears to be a post-cutoff paper on exactly drive vs decay in JEPAs. Nobody may open, cite or use it. Check the v1 date before reading anything.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

| Optimiser and schedule | SGD, momentum 0.9, lr 0.05 constant | AdamW, warm-up + cosine lr |

- **Informative direction:** Δ = mean R(Z) − mean R(N), where Z is the e = 0 row and N the never-switched row. A direction is informative iff Δ's Welch 95% CI excludes 0 and |Δ| ≥ 5; otherwise it is reported as "uninformative".
- **Equivalence:** the margin is δ = 0.2|Δ|, with sensitivity runs at 0.1 and 0.3. Row e is equivalent to N iff the Welch 90% CI of R(e) − R(N) lies within (−δ, δ), i.e. two one-sided tests at 5%. "No significant difference" is never used as equivalence.
- **Decision time D:** the smallest e in {2, 5, 10, 20} such that every row e' ≥ e is equivalent to N. D is ">20" if row 20 is not equivalent.
- **Decision curve:** f(e) = (R(e) − R(N))/Δ, with a bootstrap 95% CI over seeds.
- **Secondary analyses:**

  - D on centred RankMe;
  - D without the runs flagged as not converged (|R50 − R45| > δ/2). The primary statistic stays the epoch-50 rank.

The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.

- 34 configs × 3 seeds = 102 runs, one factor at a time.
- **Arm P** (I-JEPA recipe at 32×32: AdamW, target LayerNorm, warmup + cosine, wd 0.04→0.4, EMA 0.996→1), 21 configs:

| | GPU (Ibex V100 / RTX 2080 Ti) | CPU (`local-compute`, 8 CPUs) |

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.
issue.title: Research objective

- **T: (neither): there is no regrowth to time.** At e = 10 and 20 the segment falls by −0.0085 decades per lr_max-epoch in every window.
  - This equals the slope of one weight matrix decaying under wd_lo = 0.001 with no drive (decoupled decay, −2·lr·wd·spe/ln 10 = −0.0085).
  - That is B-iii's below-separatrix branch (g ≈ −λ_W), not slow regrowth. No horizon recovers it. B's registered premise ("lost directions re-escape under the low threshold") fails in T.
  - Switched at e = 5, the segment rises briefly to −3.30 at epoch 11, then decays.

- **References only.** The constant-lo row's rates on the same ranks bracket everything, so they decide nothing:
  - its fastest 5-epoch rate (warm-up from init) puts every row within the horizon;
  - its mean rate over 50 epochs puts every row beyond it.

- C6/N5 wording, T: "lost directions keep decaying at the low decay rate; they do not regrow". This is stronger than "not within 30–40 epochs".
- C6/N5 wording, P: "they regrow, but too slowly for the lr left in the cosine schedule (1.2–2.2× short)".

*Grid*
- **Arm T:** SGD with momentum 0.9, lr 0.05 constant, copy target, decay on every parameter, no predictor norms. Weight decay low 1e-3, high 3e-2. In E3 these gave epoch-20 counts of 39.3 ± 1.5 and 5.0.

*Statistic*
- The rank measure is the online-token count (eigenvalues ≥ 1e-3 × the largest, on 10000 test images) at epoch 50. Centred RankMe, target count and probe are reported alongside.
- **Equivalence.** A row is equivalent to the never-switched row N iff the Welch 90% CI of the difference in means lies inside ±δ (two one-sided tests at 5%). δ = 0.2·|Δ|, where Δ is the gap between the two constant rows.
- **Informative direction.** A direction counts as informative only if Δ's 95% CI excludes 0 and |Δ| ≥ 5.
- **Decision time D.** D is the earliest e such that every row e' ≥ e is equivalent to N, or ">20".
- **Decision curve.** f(e) = (R(e) − R(N))/Δ, with a bootstrap 95% CI.
- **Sensitivity checks:** margins 0.1 and 0.3; horizons at epochs 30 and 40; D on centred RankMe; D without runs flagged not converged (|R50 − R45| > δ/2).
- **Non-finite runs** are counted and excluded. A row with fewer than 4 finite seeds is "undetermined".

- The race and the μ count of the constant rows are scored in E7/C5.

*Pilot* (≤ 1 GPU-h, done: SLURM 53929960/53929961, GTX 1080 Ti, 3 runs per GPU, 1 seed, 5 epochs; development only)

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.
